title: Larkspur Health - integration call notes & next steps
content:
Call: Larkspur Health — Integration kickoff (notes / action items)
Date: 2026-05-05
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Dr. Laura Finch (Larkspur PM), Omar Vazquez (Larkspur IT), Sasha Iqbal (Larkspur Security)

High-level ask / context:
- Larkspur building patient intake triage assistant to pre-screen incoming appointment requests and surface care pathways.
- Must be HIPAA compliant; prefers Private deployment (VPC) or on-prem option.
- Target throughput: ~10k requests/day, peak concurrency ~40-60 QPS (short chat turn length avg 150 tokens).
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50 token-level preferred; 95th percentile <1.2s for typical prompts.
- Data residency: US-only; logs retained 180 days, must support log redaction and write-once audit log for compliance team.

Notes from discussion:
- Security requirements:
  - PHI cannot leave their VPC. They asked for customer-managed private deployment + KMS/HSM integration.
  - SSO is mandatory (SAML + SCIM provisioning). They use Okta.
  - Audit trails: need immutable audit log (we discussed using our private control plane + forwarding audit events to their SIEM).
  - Data retention policy: default retention 180d, with ability to purge specific records on request.
- Network and infra:
  - They'll provide a VPC peering connection; want clear list of inbound/outbound rules.
  - NAT egress for model downloads OK during setup, but afterwards minimal external egress.
  - Want TLS mutual auth for service-to-service.
- Model and serving expectations:
  - Will start with a small open model (llama2-13b-ish) and evaluate quality vs latency.
  - Interested in quantized model variants for cost control; ask for guidance on quality-tradeoffs.
  - Need model pinning and rollout capability (canary -> full) to avoid regressions in triage behavior.
- Observability / SLAs:
  - Ops team wants per-request tracing (correlate request-id to patient id in their system; note: PHI mapping rules).
  - Cost transparency required (per-token breakdown per route).
  - SLA ask: 99.9% uptime for dedicated capacity. We offered Dedicated with reserved capacity + burst.

Gotchas / open risks flagged by Larkspur:
- PHI export risk: they are worried about subtle exfiltration (attachments, phone numbers). Need auto-redaction and evaluation hooks.
- Legal: their counsel insists on a cyber-insurance clause tied to where keys are stored; if we recommend KMS integration, need to confirm supported HSM partners.
- Performance: their clinical flows include a multi-turn clarifying dialog; KV-cache warming needed to hit latency SLO for follow-ups.
- Cost predictability: they want a cost estimate for 100k tokens/day baseline and worst-case spike (3x) — need a clear bill-of-materials for Dedicated config + network costs.

Immediate technical clarifications we must get from them:
- Exact PHI categories that will appear in prompts (names, MRNs, notes) — this will drive redaction strategy.
- Whether attachments (images, PDFs) will be sent to the model. They said "maybe later" — tag as future scope.
- Preferred IdP contact for SAML test account (Okta admin).

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Maya: Share private-deploy architecture doc + VPC inbound/outbound rule template by 2026-05-07 (attach network diagram).
- Jonah: Draft Dedicated capacity recommendation (GPU type, instance counts, expected QPS and cost estimate for baseline 10k/day and 3x spike) by 2026-05-10.
- Priya: Open JIRA (JIRA-1309) capturing integration epic + compliance checklist; link to legal template for KMS/HSM by 2026-05-06.
- Larkspur (Omar): Provide sample anonymized prompt sets (5-10) and list of PHI token types by 2026-05-12.
- Security sync: schedule detailed security call between Sasha and our security lead (Ethan Cole) — propose 2026-05-11.

Follow-ups / recommended approach (SE notes):
- Recommend Private deployment in their cloud region (US-East) with customer-managed KMS. Offer optional on-prem bundle if MSA requires physical isolation.
- Suggest starting with quantized 16-bit variant for cost, run eval on triage prompts to measure regression vs FP16.
- For latency: enable continuous batching with short max-delay (10-20ms) + prefix caching for common clinical templates.
- Observability: instrument request-id propagation and provide a per-route dashboard (latency/cost/token breakdown).

Docs to send in next email (attachments):
- Private-deploy-architecture.pdf (network/VPC rules)
- Dedicated-sizing-recommendation.xlsx (baseline vs spike)
- HIPAA-integration-checklist.docx (redaction, retention, audit requirements)

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts (scratch):
- Could propose a hybrid: private control plane + dedicated inference in Larkspur VPC (gives centralized management + local data residency).
- Verify whether their counsel will accept our standard DPA with an addendum for HSM; if not, escalate to legal.
- Need SE perf test plan: synthetic load tests with representative token lengths + multi-turn flows; include KV cache warm-up scenario.

Next meeting: architecture deep-dive + security Q&A — target week of 2026-05-11 (confirm after security sync).

---
Revision log:
- 2026-05-05: initial notes and owners (Maya)
- 2026-05-06: added legal/KMS follow-up after quick sync with Priya
summary: Kickoff with Larkspur Health. They require HIPAA-compliant private deployment or on-prem, SAML/SCIM SSO, KMS/HSM integration, and latency/cost targets. Action items assigned for architecture doc, capacity sizing, legal checklist, and sample prompts.
